plan_authority: The orchestrator dispatches every pairwise-disjoint ready Build set through Codex native workers. Build and Fix launch zero lens workers. Evaluate runs a freshly computed focused quick route of exactly three or four lenses for every non-trivial task or wave, except for a closed trivial-target record or an exact authenticated expanded-route capability.

delivery_policy.design: minimum-sufficient focused quick route with solution-design coverage
delivery_policy.plan: exactly four focused quick lenses for this non-trivial plan
delivery_policy.evaluate: fresh three-or-four-lens focused quick route per non-trivial task or wave

coverage.reason: The exact-target expansion capability and bounded telemetry cross authority and privacy boundaries.
The requirement depends on deterministic, mutation, fail-closed, lifecycle, and selective-invalidation evidence.
One pure policy must remain dependency-neutral while six adapters realize all 23 approved graph edges.
Minimum-sufficient execution, the three-or-four bound, route overflow, and reuse determine the promised fan-out and token savings.

dispositions.evidence: R-0001 and its ten acceptance criteria are already approved; Plan does not reopen product desirability.
Authenticated overflow, telemetry redaction, and fail-closed authority are independently material.
The pure-module and adapter quality risks are exercised through deterministic and mutation-focused tests.
Every acceptance criterion names executable deterministic, mutation, or lifecycle evidence.
The approved Design Contract fixes the module, contract, and edge topology consumed by this Plan.
The selector operates over a fixed 26-row catalog with explicit latency and artifact bounds; no distributed scale surface is introduced.
Adapter boundaries and the final conformance join cover integration without a separate independent risk group.
Atomic route evidence, signed authority, and fail-closed reuse are part of the security-owned boundary.
LR-07 and LR-08 derive guidance from the same approved stage boundary and contract topology.
The mutation matrix and final integration selector supply the independent QA proof.
The authorized delivery excludes release, publication, deployment, and CI waiting.
No database, schema migration, or query surface is introduced.
Terminal lifecycle, fail-closed overflow, and atomic persistence are assigned to the architecture integration graph.
Dependencies, disjoint ready sets, scope ownership, and joins are explicit in the architecture-owned task graph.
No frontend behavior or interactive UI is changed.
The Python policy, adapters, control plane, and ReviewKernel are the architecture route's implementation surface.
The approved shared-policy choice and rollback boundary are fixed in the Design Contract.
Approved solution-design evidence selected the shared pure policy and incumbent adapters; Plan preserves it unchanged.
No external service, runtime dependency, or vendor is introduced.
The smallest dependency graph and parallel disjoint leaves are the same delivery-efficiency control measured by cost/fan-out.
Twenty-three approved edges cross policy, loop, review, authority, telemetry, tests, roles, and documentation.
No mobile runtime or presentation surface is changed.
No interactive or rendered UI behavior is introduced; documentation remains plain semantic text.
Bounded redaction, pseudonymous targets, and private-path refusal are explicit security-owned tests.
The feature's purpose and hard acceptance bounds are worker fan-out, token use, reuse, and overflow cost.
No locale-sensitive user text, formatting, pluralization, or translation contract is changed.

criteria: AC-LR6: Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate each emit exactly one internally consistent evidenced disposition for every catalog lens, and only execute_deep/execute_light launch workers; verify missing, duplicate, unsupported, and unevidenced rows fail closed.

AC-LR8: Equal canonical inputs and policy version produce the same ordered route, dispositions, and fingerprint for all routed stages; verify repeats, key-order variance, relevant-input change, and policy-version change.

tasks.gap: Review adapter must normalize ordinary dependency-impact maps with integer depth keys before strict canonical route fingerprinting.
criteria: AC-LR4: Every non-trivial task or wave Evaluate executes exactly three or four lenses from actual diff, changed files, dependency impact, test evidence, and unresolved findings; verify material evidence changes alter the route.

AC-LR7: A material Fix invalidates and reruns only lens evidence whose canonical fingerprint inputs changed while unchanged evidence is reused without launching a worker; verify single-input, multi-input, and unchanged cases.

AC-LR5: Plan/Evaluate with more than four independent mandatory risks splits scope or refuses pending authenticated expanded-route approval listing extra lenses and cost; verify no silent drop and reject tampered approval.

AC-LR9: Each route records stage, selected count, reasons, estimated/actual tokens, runtime, cache reuse, and invalidation cause with bounded redaction; verify schema completeness and privacy behavior.

AC-LR10: Successful, failed, cancelled, interrupted, and handed-off Build/Fix attempts launch zero lens workers, with lens execution confined to Product, Design, Plan, and Evaluate; verify native-dispatch traces.
